answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (source: `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>`, read-only; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, LBNL/NCEDC catalogue, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5) — Sigma and P(Mw >= 5.5) per year per b scenario:
- b = 1.0: Sigma = -5.449, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198 (P over observed volume = 5.236e-06), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719.
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922 (volume = 0.0002155), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809.
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474 (volume = 0.0006484), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653.

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at/above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts): b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842.

Which is which: the per-b table above is the CALIBRATED estimate (LBNL catalogue magnitudes, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5), giving P(Mw>=5.5) of roughly 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year across b = 1.0 to 0.65. The single DAS-based number (P = 0.07842/yr at b = 0.9849) is an UPPER BOUND with uncalibrated magnitudes that over-counts events, so the calibrated catalogue-based probabilities are the meaningful ones — under all three b scenarios a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event at Brady Hot Springs in March 2016 is very unlikely per year.
